findings.title: Possible hardcoded credential (AWS access key ID)
findings.explanation: This added line matches the format of a real credential. Secrets committed to source control are exposed to everyone with read access and remain in git history even after removal.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the value, load it from an environment variable or secret manager, and rotate the credential if it was ever valid.

findings.title: Shell command built with string interpolation
findings.explanation: `exec`/`execSync` run their argument through a shell. Interpolating values into the command string allows command injection if any value can be influenced by a user.
findings.suggestedFix: Use `execFile`/`spawn` with an argument array (no shell), or strictly validate every interpolated value.

findings.title: TLS certificate verification disabled
findings.explanation: Disabling certificate verification lets anyone on the network path impersonate the server and read or modify the traffic.
findings.evidence: return new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true, rejectUnauthorized: false });
findings.suggestedFix: Keep verification enabled. For private certificate authorities, pass the CA certificate (for example via the `ca` option or NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS) instead.

findings.title: Dynamic code execution
findings.explanation: `eval`, `new Function` and string arguments to `setTimeout`/`setInterval` execute arbitrary code. If any part of the string can be influenced by input, this is a code-injection vector; it also defeats static analysis.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace with explicit logic (for example a lookup table or `JSON.parse` for data), or pass a function instead of a string to timers.

findings.title: Focused test left in code
findings.explanation: `.only` (or `fit`/`fdescribe`) makes the test runner skip every other test in the file or suite, so CI can pass while most tests silently do not run.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove `.only` (or rename `fit`/`fdescribe` back to `it`/`describe`) before merging.

findings.title: Debugger statement left in code
findings.explanation: A `debugger` statement pauses execution whenever developer tools or an inspector are attached, and is almost always a leftover from debugging.

limitations: Only added lines are analyzed, line by line, with a fixed rule set; issues that depend on wider context are not detected.
